question: Which specific hormone is primarily responsible for smooth muscle relaxation throughout the gastrointestinal tract during pregnancy?
explanation: Progesterone acts widely as a smooth muscle relaxant, significantly decreasing the tone and motility of the gastrointestinal tract during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary mechanical cause of intra-abdominal organ displacement during the later stages of gestation?
explanation: As pregnancy progresses, the growing uterus takes up most of the pelvic and abdominal cavity, physically shifting the stomach, intestines, and other organs upward. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary physiological mechanism behind pregnancy-related heartburn (pyrosis)?

options.B: Hypersecretion of hydrochloric acid by parietal cells
options.C: Rapid emptying of stomach contents into the jejunum
options.D: Relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter

explanation: Progesterone relaxes the lower esophageal sphincter, permitting acidic gastric juices to splash backward into the esophagus and cause a burning sensation. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h2)

question: A woman in her second trimester complains of frequent burning chest discomfort after meals. Which advice is most clinically appropriate?

options.A: Increase intake of citrus fruits and spicy foods to stimulate digestion
options.B: Restrict fluid intake drastically throughout the entire day
options.C: Lie flat on the back for thirty minutes following every meal
options.D: Eat smaller, more frequent meals and avoid lying down immediately afterward

explanation: Smaller meals reduce gastric volume and pressure against the relaxed sphincter, while an upright posture uses gravity to prevent acid reflux. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h2)

question: Why does prolonged transit time in the large intestine lead directly to constipation during pregnancy?

options.B: The large intestine ceases all bacterial activity entirely
options.C: Bile salts precipitate and block the anal canal
options.D: Increased water absorption makes the stool hard and dry

explanation: When bowel transit slows down, feces remain in the colon longer, allowing excessive water to be reabsorbed and resulting in hard, difficult-to-pass stools. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following conditions is a direct vascular complication commonly triggered by pregnancy-induced constipation and pelvic venous stasis?
explanation: Straining against hard stools combined with high pelvic venous pressure causes the rectal veins to engorge and form hemorrhoids. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary effect of progesterone on the gallbladder during pregnancy?
explanation: Progesterone relaxes the smooth muscle of the biliary tree, causing the gallbladder to empty incompletely and predisposing the woman to stasis and gallstones. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h4)

question: Which normal laboratory value typically increases significantly during a healthy pregnancy due to placental contribution?
explanation: Alkaline phosphatase rises progressively because the placenta produces its own isoenzyme form of this alkaline phosphatase enzyme. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h4)

question: What happens to gastric motility and emptying during active labour?

options.A: It reverses completely, causing continuous emesis
options.B: It virtually ceases or becomes extremely sluggish
options.C: It remains entirely unaffected by contractions
options.D: It accelerates dramatically to clear the abdomen

explanation: Stress, pain, and labour medications inhibit gastrointestinal motility, causing food and fluids to remain in the stomach for long periods. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary clinical danger associated with continued oral intake of solid foods during established labour?

options.A: Aspiration pneumonia if vomiting occurs under anesthesia
options.B: Premature rupture of membranes due to abdominal pressure
options.C: Severe electrolyte imbalances from rapid dehydration

explanation: Because the stomach does not empty during labour, food remains inside, increasing the risk of inhaling gastric acid into the lungs if emesis occurs during an anesthetic induction. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h5)

question: Which hormonal shift triggers the reversal of gastrointestinal relaxation immediately after delivery?

options.A: A massive spike in human placental lactogen
options.B: An abrupt cessation of thyroid hormone production
options.C: A sharp drop in progesterone and relaxin levels
options.D: A sustained surge in circulating estrogen

explanation: Delivery of the placenta removes the primary source of progesterone and relaxin, initiating the return of normal muscle tone across the digestive tract. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h6)

question: What is a major psychological and physical barrier to normal bowel elimination in the immediate postpartum period?

options.A: Fear of pain from perineal lacerations or episiotomy repairs
options.B: Complete physical paralysis of the large intestine
options.C: Total absence of peristalsis lasting for at least three weeks
options.D: Permanent closure of the anal sphincter muscles

explanation: Pain from perineal wounds or hemorrhoids causes women to suppress the urge to defaecate, which worsens constipation after birth. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h6)

question: A postpartum woman on her second day after a spontaneous vaginal delivery expresses deep reluctance to use the toilet because she fears her stitches will tear. What is the best initial nursing intervention?

options.A: Administer an immediate high-pressure tap water enema to force evacuation
options.B: Instruct her to restrict all fluid intake until the perineum heals completely
options.C: Reassure her, explain that stitches will not break from normal straining, and encourage adequate fluids and fiber
options.D: Insert a rigid rectal tube to manually empty the lower bowel

explanation: Reassurance combined with non-pharmacological comfort measures and stool softeners helps alleviate anxiety and promotes safe, natural bowel elimination. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h7)

question: What is a key nursing responsibility regarding gastrointestinal health during the intrapartum period?

options.A: Administering strong laxatives to every woman entering the labour ward
options.B: Checking serum liver enzyme levels every fifteen minutes
options.C: Encouraging a heavy, high-fat meal to maintain maternal energy
options.D: Monitoring and restricting oral intake to prevent aspiration risks

explanation: Because gastric emptying stops during labour, nurses must regulate oral intake carefully to guard against aspiration pneumonia. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h7)
